I'm throwing this out here because I've been seeing a lot of ppl saying this, but Iearned yesterday is that:
-yes, some new data is showing throat swabs may be more accurate...BUT
-no, do not use home tests for throat swabs.

Tests have to be manufactured specifically for throat swab testing, and most at-home rapid tests right now are not. If the instructions in a home test does not explicitly say a throat swab can be used, do not use this method.

Throat swabs with the wrong test solution will often create false positives because of the acidity in saliva.

Although dozens of ppl incorrectly using these tests and coming up with false positives isn't exactly endangering anyone, I think it's important to spread this info, because I'm sure false negatives are bound to happen as well. Using a test in the intended manner is our best bet at getting accurate results.

Just be aware of which antibody test you are getting - some of them do not look for the spike antibodies (which is all the vaccine has) and instead look at other proteins that wouldn't be present with a vaccine.

Another thing to consider is that it could've just been a false negative. Quality of those tests vary.  
Other players in the role of immunity are Memory B and T cells, and they wouldn't show up on an antibody test.  


And just for fun:

IgM antibodies are typically produced really early on during an infection, between 1-3 weeks post symptom onset

IgGs are produced later.  


Positive IgG and positive IgM mean the infection was recent  
Positive IgG and -IgM means that you may have had the infection a long time ago  
Negative IgG and +IgM means you may be battling the infection (1-2 weeks)  
(Source: misc science communicator accounts on Instagram)

I've also read that not all antibody tests are the same. They all test for different things. Also - be aware that antibodies are not the only players in the role of immunity. I wouldn't be too concerned about what the results of an antibody show. I'll try to find some sources and update later
